name: Shiza Charania
title: Founder
conviction_themes: Humanoid robots are among the most advanced and impactful platforms worth building on
The barrier to training and deploying custom ML models has dropped from needing a team to needing just curiosity and determination
Robotics deployment requires a fundamentally different skill set than robotics research — operators and industrialists, not just roboticists
Building hands-on projects and surrounding yourself with smart people is the core operating philosophy
previous_experiences: Joined 1X as a mechanical engineer on the joints and body team, contributing to subsystem development on humanoid robots
Conducted biomedical imaging research at University Health Network, co-developing 3D brain tumour segmentation models
Won 'Outstanding in AI – Young AI Role Model of the Year' award in North America
Published a machine learning article and wrote for the AI Accelerator Institute
Participated in The Knowledge Society (TKS) as an AI innovator building computer vision and healthcare projects

Built GitHub projects spanning brain tumour segmentation, MNIST, sycophancy research in LLMs, mechanistic interpretability (logit-tuned lens), schizophrenia EEG, and embedded hardware (Rubik's cube macropad, dual-axis solar panel)
bio_text: Shiza Charania is a Toronto-based founder of Haptile, coming from a mechanical engineering role at humanoid robotics company 1X. She has a background spanning biomedical imaging research, ML research on LLM sycophancy and mechanistic interpretability, and early AI innovation through The Knowledge Society, and was recognized as a Young AI Role Model of the Year in North America. She is hands-on across hardware and software, operating at the intersection of robotics, haptics, and applied ML.
